actions.detail: First pre-serve hand bounce: at 0.0-0.2 s the athlete holds the ball in his left (non-racket) hand at chest height while bent over the racket hand; at 0.4 s the left arm extends down and the ball is seen falling near knee level; at 0.6-0.8 s the ball is at/near the court surface and rebounding; by 1.0-1.2 s the ball is back at the left hand and held. Exact ground-contact frame is approximate because the small yellow ball is hard to track against the dark court.

Second pre-serve hand bounce: ball held in left hand at 1.2-1.4 s; at 1.6 s the hand drops and the ball is seen falling; at 1.8-2.0 s the ball is at the surface; at 2.2 s it rebounds toward the hand. By 2.4 s the athlete is upright with both hands on the racket, so the catch/pocketing of the ball after this bounce is not clearly visible - the bounce count is inferred from the two release-rebound cycles.

Service toss: after a held ready/preparation stance (2.4-4.8 s, out of scope), at 5.0 s the athlete stands and tilts his head up; at 5.2-5.4 s the left (non-racket) arm extends fully overhead and releases the ball, which then leaves view against the black background. The toss release moment (~5.2-5.4 s) is inferred from arm extension since the ball itself is not visible in flight.

Racket-arm upward swing: at 5.4-5.6 s the right (racket) arm is dropped back with the racket blurred behind the body (trophy/drop phase); at 5.8 s the racket accelerates up beside the head; at 6.0 s the racket is at the top of the overhead arc with the arm extended. Ball contact at the apex cannot be confirmed because the ball is invisible against the dark backdrop.

Follow-through and landing: at 6.2 s the racket is still overhead and blurred; at 6.4-6.6 s the torso rotates forward and the racket arm sweeps across the body to the left side; at 6.8 s the racket finishes low across the hips as the athlete lands from the serve motion; by 7.0 s he is in a crouched recovery position. The stroke completion is visible, though the instant of ball impact remains unconfirmed.

actions.detail: Complete service stroke: initiated with the head-up preparation and left-arm toss (5.0-5.4 s), continued through the racket-arm drop and overhead upward swing (5.4-6.0 s), and finished with the cross-body follow-through, landing and recovery crouch (6.0-7.0 s), after which the athlete moves forward (7.2-7.6 s). Spin, grip, and ball contact cannot be verified from the muted, dark-background footage; the serve is established from the full observable kinetic chain (toss -> overhead swing -> follow-through -> landing).

A male voice says "a sacar." (0.0-1.28s) and a sharp click sounds (0.168-0.218s) as an athlete performs two pre-serve hand bounces with his non-racket left arm, dropping the ball to the court surface at 0.4-1.2s and again at 1.6-2.4s.

After holding a ready stance, the athlete initiates a complete service stroke starting at 5.0s: he tosses the ball overhead with his left arm (5.0-5.4s), swings the racket upward with his right arm (5.4-6.0s), and executes a cross-body follow-through while landing into a crouched recovery position by 7.0s.
